rv.q: And what a welcome addition to the programme it is. After wandering along a winding path through the trees, you arrive at a pine-built Pavilion. Devine greets you at the door and ushers you inside, into a cosy room cluttered with images and items from her life: a typewriter, a record, a pair of shoes.

A slightly extended duration, or a more adventurous integration of the visual field towards the climax, might have pushed this fascinating experiment from a superb fringe-style curiosity into an entirely transcendent masterpiece.
I found the whole thing lacked cohesion and purpose.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this immersive outdoor experience: one praises its persuasive case for surrendering personal space in nature, while another finds the self-discovery journey less compelling despite gentle, caring facilitation.
